metaTitle: Protect Devices That Can't Protect Themselves | SecuEdge
metaDescription: Cameras, sensors, medical devices and machines kept on their own network, watched and controlled.

hero.headline: Protect the devices that can't protect themselves.
hero.sub: Cameras, sensors, medical devices and machines kept on their own network, watched and controlled.

challenges.title: Weak devices, open doors
challenges.desc: Connected devices often run old software and cannot install security tools. Left on the main network, one weak device can open the door to everything else.

challenges.title: Unpatchable devices
challenges.desc: Cameras and machines run old software that cannot take security tools.

challenges.title: Always on, always exposed
challenges.desc: Devices that never sleep give attackers an always-open door.

approach.title: Separate device networks
approach.desc: Separate networks for cameras, sensors, medical devices and machines.

approach.title: Outbound control
approach.desc: Rules that stop devices calling out to places they should not.

approach.title: Intrusion prevention on device traffic
approach.desc: Intrusion prevention on traffic to and from devices.

approach.title: Per-device view
approach.desc: A per-device view of what each device is doing.

indiaContext: Device logs stay in India by default.

process.title: Identify
process.desc: We learn how your network is used: how many people, which sites, which systems matter most.

process.title: Analyze
process.desc: We recommend the right model and settings for your risks and your industry.

process.title: Protect
process.desc: Our team or partner sets up SecuEdge Frontier and trains your team.

process.title: Adapt
process.desc: Regular updates, quarterly security reviews and 24/7 India-based support keep you protected as things change.

faqs.q: Do I need to install anything on the devices?
faqs.a: No. Protection is applied at the network.

faqs.q: Can I see every device on the network?
faqs.a: The dashboard shows active devices and their traffic.
Yes. Keeping machine (OT) and office (IT) networks apart is one of the most common uses.
In India, by default. Traffic, logs and policy data stay on Indian soil, with no overseas routing.
